core_intuitions: The vocabulary is a fixed, frozen ID LAYOUT: ids 0-255 are raw UTF-8 bytes, 256..32758 are learned BPE merges, and the top 9 slots are reserved special tokens in a fixed order -- and once training begins, id 32763 means '<|user|>' for every checkpoint forever, so the layout (and every special token the project will ever need) must be decided UP FRONT.

Vocab size is a BUDGET LINE ITEM that competes directly with depth: the tied embedding table costs V x d_model params, so against a fixed ~100M budget a bigger vocabulary literally subtracts transformer layers -- GPT-2's 50,257 vocab would eat ~a quarter of the budget, on the order of four whole layers.

Tied embeddings make ONE V x d_model matrix do two jobs (input token lookup AND output logit projection), saving V x d_model params -- at Stack-100M's scale roughly 6 layers of depth, for one line of code.

The efficient trainer turns an O(merges x corpus) rescan into seconds by only TOUCHING THE WORDS THAT CONTAIN THE MERGED PAIR (an inverted pair->words index) and finding the current best pair in O(log n) (a lazy-deleted max-heap whose stale entries are discarded on pop, never decrease-keyed).

Vocab size is a genuine tradeoff curve, not a free knob: a bigger vocab compresses better (fewer tokens per document) but spends more embedding params; a smaller vocab buys back layers but pays it back in longer sequences and more forward passes per document, every training step for the life of the run.

new_figures.name: vocab-vs-depth-budget-lever
new_figures.concept: A fixed ~100M-parameter budget drawn as a constant-length bar: as vocab_size grows, the tied embedding table (V x d_model) claims more of the bar and fewer transformer-layer blocks fit -- vocabulary size literally trades against depth.
new_figures.rationale: This IS the argument the chapter exists to make ('vocabulary size is not a free hyperparameter... it is a line item that competes directly with depth and width for the same fixed budget'). The chapter carries it entirely in a numeric table; a single constant-length-bar comparison makes 'the lever slides params between embedding and depth' viscerally geometric in one glance -- the reader SEES the layer blocks pop off as the embedding segment grows. Nothing else in the chapter conveys the thesis visually.
new_figures.placement: ## Vocab Size Is a Design Lever at 100M Parameters (anchor after the tradeoff table under '### The tradeoff table', before '### Why 32,768 and not smaller')
new_figures.brief: A vertical stack of horizontal bars, one row per vocab_size scenario from the chapter's own table, all bars EXACTLY THE SAME TOTAL LENGTH to encode 'fixed ~100M budget'. Put a caption above the stack: 'Same total length = fixed ~100M budget. The only choice is how to split it.' Rows top-to-bottom: 8,192 / 16,384 / 32,768 (Stack-100M, highlighted) / 50,257 (GPT-2) / 100,277. Each bar is split into two clearly labeled segments: LEFT = 'tied embedding table (V x 512)', its length proportional to V; RIGHT = 'transformer blocks', drawn NOT as a solid fill but as a row of small identical square cells, one cell per affordable layer (each cell = one ~2.82M-param block), so the count is literally countable. As V grows down the stack the left segment lengthens and the number of right-hand cells visibly drops: ~34, ~33, ~30, ~26, ~17 cells respectively (use the chapter's 'layers affordable' numbers). Label each embedding segment with its share of budget from the chapter (4.2%, 8.4%, 16.8%, 25.7%, 51.3%). Visually emphasize the 32,768 row as the chosen baseline (heavier border / a small 'Stack-100M' tag). Draw one bold callout bracket spanning the difference between the 32,768 and 50,257 rows' layer cells: 'GPT-2's vocab costs ~4 whole transformer layers of depth.' Use only the integers already in the chapter; theme-safe muted fills for the two segment types (no hardcoded brand primaries), a consistent distinct tint for 'embedding' vs 'layer cells'. All labels inside the viewBox, clear top-to-bottom reading order, legible in light and dark.

new_figures.name: bpe-trainer-incremental-merge
new_figures.concept: The efficient trainer's core trick: pop the top pair from a lazy-deleted max-heap in O(log n), then use an inverted pair->words index to re-tokenize ONLY the handful of words that actually contain that pair, leaving the rest of the corpus untouched -- instead of a full-corpus rescan every merge.
new_figures.rationale: The chapter's whole engineering claim ('turning a multi-hour job into single-digit seconds', 3.25s for 32,503 merges) rests on two data-structure ideas that are inherently spatial-and-temporal: which words a merge touches, and how the heap avoids decrease-key via lazy deletion. A static frame conveys 'only affected words are touched'; the animation of one merge cycle makes the lazy-deletion discard-on-pop and the localized fuse-and-repush loop click in a way the dense code comments cannot. This is the second load-bearing intuition of the chapter and currently has no visual.
new_figures.placement: ## A From-Scratch, Efficient Byte-Level BPE Trainer (anchor after the paragraph ending '...an O(log n) heap pop instead of an O(n) linear scan.', before the tokenizer.py code block)
new_figures.brief: Three linked panels left-to-right, with a headline caption on top: 'Naive: rescan ALL words every merge = O(merges x corpus). Here: pop best pair in O(log n), touch only the words that contain it.' PANEL 1 (the heap): a small vertical priority queue of entries '(count, pair)' sorted with the largest count on top, e.g. top entry '(9, t+h)'. Show ONE lower entry struck-through / greyed and tagged 'stale: count no longer matches pair_counts -> discarded on pop (lazy deletion, no decrease-key)'. PANEL 2 (the inverted index): a compact 3-4 row table 'pair -> {word indices}', with the row for the popped pair (t,h) -> {2, 5, 9} highlighted and an arrow labeled 'only these word ids' pointing to panel 3. PANEL 3 (the corpus): a column of ~7 word rows, each word drawn as a strip of small symbol-id cells; HIGHLIGHT only rows 2, 5, 9 as 'touched this merge' and grey out the rest with a large label 'untouched -- never rescanned'. In the touched rows, show the adjacent cells 't','h' about to fuse into one new cell labeled 'id 256+i'. ANIMATION (enhancement; the first static frame must already tell the whole story): step through ONE merge cycle -- (1) pop top of heap; (2) a stale pop appears first and is flicked away as 'discarded'; (3) the real best pair is verified (small check 'heap count == live count'); (4) the inverted-index row lights up and arrows shoot only to word rows 2/5/9; (5) in those rows the 't'+'h' cells merge into a single new-id cell; (6) fresh '(count, pair)' entries get pushed back onto the heap. Then the loop restarts with the next-best pair. Keep counts as small illustrative integers (e.g. 9, 5, 2); do NOT print the chapter's 3.25s timing inside the figure -- keep it schematic. Theme-safe muted colors, everything inside the viewBox, no overlapping labels, readable identically in light and dark.

new_figures.name: vocab-id-layout-frozen
new_figures.concept: The permanent id map: [0-255] raw bytes, [256-32758] learned merges, [32759-32767] the 9 special tokens in fixed order -- with the arithmetic M = V - 256 - S = 32,503, and why adding a token after the fact invalidates every checkpoint.
new_figures.rationale: The chapter's first design commitment is 'reserve every special token up front, in a fixed order' because the layout is frozen the moment training starts ('id 32763 IS the concept of <|user|> for every checkpoint we will ever produce'). The book currently renders this only as an ASCII strip and a table. A clean segmented number line that expands the 9 special slots and shows the 'add-a-token-later shifts everything -> checkpoints meaningless' failure mode makes the permanence argument -- the emotional core of 'reserve now' -- concrete.
new_figures.placement: ## Reserving Special Tokens Up Front (anchor after the ASCII 'id: 0 ... 32767' strip and the M = V - 256 - S equation, before the '!!! tip' aside)
new_figures.brief: A horizontal segmented number line spanning id 0 to 32767, divided into three proportional regions with labels below: [0-255] 'raw UTF-8 bytes -- fixed, universal (id == byte value)'; [256-32758] '32,503 learned BPE merges -- trained on the Stack-100M mix'; [32759-32767] '9 reserved special tokens -- fixed order'. Draw a zoom/callout expanding the tiny top region into 9 labeled slots in exact order with their ids: <|bos|> 32759, <|eos|> 32760, <|pad|> 32761, <|system|> 32762, <|user|> 32763, <|assistant|> 32764, <|end|> 32765, <|tool_call|> 32766, <|tool_result|> 32767. Print the arithmetic as an annotation: 'M = V - 256 - S = 32,768 - 256 - 9 = 32,503 merges'. Add a permanence banner: 'Frozen once training begins -- id 32763 = <|user|> for every checkpoint, forever.' Then a small CONTRAST inset panel titled 'Why reserve UP FRONT': show the same strip but with a new token inserted mid-range, all ids above it shoved right by one, and a muted-warning marker over the merges region reading 'every id shifted -> every checkpoint's embedding rows now point at the wrong token -> meaningless'. Use the exact ids/integers from the chapter; theme-safe fills (a distinct muted tint per region, warning shown via pattern/outline not a hardcoded red), all labels inside the viewBox and legible in both themes.

new_figures.name: tied-embeddings-one-matrix-two-jobs
new_figures.concept: Weight tying: a single V x d_model matrix serves both the input embedding lookup and the output logit projection, so its parameters are paid once instead of twice -- worth ~6 layers of depth at Stack-100M's scale.
new_figures.rationale: The chapter calls tied embeddings 'non-negotiable' and quantifies it as ~6 free layers, but presents it purely as prose plus a worked equation. A compact 'one matrix, two jobs' diagram plus a tiny untied-vs-tied before/after makes the parameter double-spend -- and what it buys back in depth -- immediately legible, reinforcing the budget-lever thesis of the chapter's second half. Lower priority than the two mechanisms above but a clean, self-contained intuition.
new_figures.placement: ### Tied embeddings: the first lever (anchor after the '!!! example "Worked example: what tying is worth, in layers"' block)
new_figures.brief: Center the figure on a single matrix block labeled 'E : 32,768 x 512  (16.8M params)'. Two paths emanate from it: (1) INPUT path -- an arrow from a token id into E showing 'row lookup: token id -> 512-dim vector'; (2) OUTPUT path -- an arrow from a 512-dim hidden state through 'E^T' producing '32,768 logits (distribution over next token)'. Caption between them: 'same weights, two jobs (Press & Wolf, 2017)'. Below, a small before/after comparison using two proportional bars: UNTIED = two separate matrices, bar labeled '2 x 16.8M = 33.6M params'; TIED = one matrix, bar half as long labeled '16.8M params'. A bold arrow between them: 'saved 16.8M params ~= 6 transformer layers of depth, for one line: lm_head.weight = embed.weight'. Optionally a faint one-line footnote nodding at the tension the chapter raises: 'the catch: one 512-dim space now does double duty (softmax bottleneck).' summary: This capstone tokenizer chapter is concept-rich but has ZERO figures -- it carries every mechanism in prose, ASCII strips, and one numeric table. Nothing to audit (existing = []). It has two truly foundational, currently-invisible intuitions plus two strong supporting ones, so I propose four figures, disciplined to the chapter's actual load-bearing ideas. P1 #1 (vocab-vs-depth-budget-lever, static): the chapter's THESIS -- constant-length bars for a fixed ~100M budget where the tied embedding segment grows and countable per-layer cells pop off as vocab_size climbs 8k->16k->32k->50k->100k, making 'GPT-2's vocab = ~4 layers of depth' geometric rather than tabular. P1 #2 (bpe-trainer-incremental-merge, animated): the chapter's ENGINEERING claim -- a heap + inverted-index + corpus triptych showing that a merge touches only the words containing the popped pair (rest greyed 'never rescanned'), with an animated single-merge cycle that surfaces lazy-deletion discard-on-pop and the localized fuse-and-repush loop; the static frame alone conveys 'only affected words are touched'. P2 #3 (vocab-id-layout-frozen, static): a segmented 0..32767 number line with the 9 special slots expanded and a contrast inset showing that inserting a token later shifts every id and invalidates every checkpoint -- the permanence argument behind 'reserve up front'. P3 #4 (tied-embeddings-one-matrix-two-jobs, static): 'one V x d matrix, two jobs' plus an untied-vs-tied bar showing the double-spend and the ~6 layers it buys back. All briefs use only the chapter's own integers (no invented benchmarks), specify theme-safe muted fills, and are fully understandable as static frames with animation as enhancement only.
